claims.text: The Atacama Desert lies mainly in northern Chile.
Peru, Argentina and Bolivia each contain far less of the Atacama Desert than Chile does.
Scientists have used the Atacama's dry, Mars-like soils to test instruments for Mars rovers.
Major observatories, including ALMA, operate in the Atacama because of its clear, dry skies.

evidence.restatement: The Atacama lies in northern Chile between the Andes and the Pacific.
Only fringes of the Atacama, under its broader definitions, reach Peru, Bolivia and Argentina.
NASA and other teams have tested Mars rover instruments in the Atacama's Mars-like soils.
ALMA and other major observatories were built in the Atacama for its dry, clear skies.
The Atacama Desert is a coastal strip mainly in northern Chile.
Only marginal parts of the Atacama (southern Peru, south-west Bolivia, north-west Argentina by some definitions) lie outside Chile.
Teams including NASA's have tested Mars rover and life-detection instruments in the hyper-arid Atacama soils.
ALMA and the European Southern Observatory's Paranal site operate in the Atacama because of its dry, clear air.
